report:
Summary: The B−A residual difference is concentrated on the earliest token positions (especially pos0, also pos1) in deeper layers, and the logit-lens vocabulary those difference vectors point toward is strongly biased toward “news/headline” and vivid/sensational vocabulary (words like tragic/tragedy, iconic, vivid/colorful, victims/refugees/heard, coming/headlines/Driver/Names, refused/blitz/worst, optimize/strive/try). That pattern supports the simple interpretation that Model B (relative to A) boosts logits for newsy/sensational/descriptive tokens at the start of a sequence.

Why I conclude that
- Spatial pattern: the L2 norm is dominated by pos0 (and pos1) in late layers (layers ~18–25, with a very large peak at layer 25 pos0). That is where prediction effects for the next token are most likely to be formed, so this difference will change early-token predictions/style.
- Lexical pattern: the logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm cells show a repeated cluster of tokens across many deep (layer,pos) cells: “tragic”, “tragedy”, “iconic”, “vivid/colourful/vibrant”, “heard”, “victims/refugees”, “headlines/Coming/Driver/Names”, and related negative/sensational adjectives (“worst”, “refused”, “shocked”, “blitz”). Those are coherent semantically (newsy, dramatic, vivid descriptions / headlines).
- Consistency across layers/positions: the same semantic theme appears in many different deep layer cells and multiple positions (pos0–pos4), which makes a random noise explanation unlikely.

Caveats / limits
- I cannot say why the difference exists (e.g., changed pretraining mixture, a style fine-tune, safety filter differences, or a calibration change). The evidence supports a lexical/style shift but not a specific training objective.
- Earlier/mid layers show some unrelated tokens (e.g., “ Sale”, “rock”, “på”) — but the dominant, coherent signal is the news/sensational vocabulary in deep pos0/pos1 cells.
- Patchscope continuations were not provided, so I can’t show direct continuation-level behavior changes; the claim is based on decoding the residual-difference vectors (logit lens).

Short conclusion: The evidence supports naming a specific difference at the lexical/style level: Model B (relative to A) increases activation components that push logits toward newsy, vivid/sensational/headline-type tokens at the start of sequences. I cannot infer a more specific training objective or motivation from the provided data.
